author: Justin
text:
<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Harry</custom> <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Mon</custom> — planning OMH-711; tracing the legacy code shows "app-download" is actually two different things. I need the history + current state to settle the v2 migration scope and whether the `/common/ums/send` blocker even applies.

**Current behavior (code-verified)**

1. **Routed page** `/app-download` (`pages/app-download`): no content — on init it sniffs the user-agent and redirects (Android → Play Store, iOS → App Store), then calls `window.close()`. Empty markup.
2. **SMS send-link form + QR** (`shared/bottom-contents/app-download`, selector `app-app-download`): posts `/common/ums/send`. But it is commented out in `bottom-contents.component.html:15` — disabled since 2025-08-07 (`becab4599`, "add new UI"). Not rendered on any live route.

**Access paths**

* No in-app link or navigation to the PC `/app-download` route (the footer block that embedded it is commented out; no header/menu link) — direct URL only.
* The SMS body links to `https://m.ohmyhotel.com/app-download` (mobile domain, not PC); the QR encodes `${diffPlatformDomain}/app-download` (mobile, from PC's side). Both target mobile — and both live inside the disabled block.

**Questions**

1. **History —** what was the original goal of the "enter phone number → SMS the app-download link" design? And was commenting it out on 2025-08-07 an intentional deprecation, or a temporary step during a redesign ("add new UI")?
2. **Current state —** is the PC `/app-download` store-redirector still a valid entry point? Is app-download inducement effectively mobile-only now?
3. **countryPhoneCode / BE schema —** since the form is already disabled, is there any reason to resurrect it and finalize the `/common/ums/send` schema in v2? (If dropped, the flag-ON BE-schema blocker dissolves.)
4. **Migration direction —** (a) migrate only the store-redirector route and drop the dead form; (b) resurrect the form (needs the BE schema); (c) don't keep a PC app-download content page at all — which do you prefer?

**If you confirm deprecation:** I'll drop the SMS form from OMH-711's scope and remove the flag-ON BE-schema blocker, and post a correction on OMH-605 B3 — its TRACK verdict rested on a now-stale "LIVE in PC" premise (the `sendLink` caller has been commented out since 2025-08-07), so `/common/ums/send` becomes EXCLUDE like B1/B2.

author: Mon
text:
Hi <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Justin</custom> ,Thanks for the detailed trace. Here is my answers:

**1. History / comment-out:** The comment-out was intentional, and the SMS send-link form is now fully unused. That code is dead — it can be cleaned up.

**2. Current state:** Yes, the PC `/app-download` store-redirector is still a valid entry point.

**3. countryPhoneCode / BE schema:** I'd suggest keeping the `/common/ums/send` API itself. B2C no longer uses it, but the Partner site currently uses it for Voucher and Invoice booking (send flows). So please don't mark it EXCLUDE on the BE side — it just falls out of OMH-711's scope.

**4. Migration direction:** I think option **(a)** — migrate only the store-redirector route and drop the dead form — is the optimal choice at this point.

So from my side: drop the SMS form from OMH-711's scope and remove the flag-ON BE-schema blocker. Just note on OMH-605 B3 that the endpoint stays alive for the Partner site rather than becoming EXCLUDE.

author: Justin
text:
**Scope addition — web-pc (v2) enters scope (2026-07-03, from OMH-748).**

The current "Out" section scopes this Epic to legacy-pc (mobile/hana/native/backend are separately tracked); web-pc (the v2 React app) was implicitly out because it had no secrets. **That changes with the OMH-748 build-approach decision**: v2 login ships in the **same client-side form as legacy first** (replicating legacy's client-side OAuth handling, since legacy already ships those secrets in its bundle — v2 matching it is no worse than today's posture). That makes **web-pc a new holder of the same client-bundle OAuth/PG secret debt**.

**Implication for this Epic's Stage B/C**: when PG hash generation and the Kakao OAuth `client_secret` exchange are relocated server-side, the fix must migrate **legacy-pc AND web-pc together** — do not remediate legacy while leaving the v2 copies exposed. Acceptance criteria 1–3 (no secrets in any prod client bundle; PG hashing server-side; OAuth secret never browser-delivered) should be read as applying to **both** apps once web-pc's login lands.

Recorded in: OMH-748 (BUILD APPROACH + dependency note), OMH-457 Epic body, `docs/migration/v2-migration-plan.md` §7. No action needed until OMH-748 ships v2 login; flagged now so the Stage B child tickets don't miss web-pc.

author: Justin
text:
**This ticket is now a SEQUENCING GATE for the route-flip roadmap** (recorded 2026-07-03 during the OMH-709/710 shell review; also in `docs/migration/v2-migration-plan.md` §7).

**Why**: during the Strangler period the login UI (`LoginModalComponent`) exists only inside legacy-booted pages — an Angular component can never mount over a v2 document. v2 pages hand off to the guarded `/my-page/booking-history` (legacy `auth-guard.service.ts:103` auto-opens the real login modal and stores `returnUrl`; changed from the home-page handoff so the flow is one step: click → page turn → modal). The domain cookie crossover (`{hostname}_userToken`) carries the session back to v2 — already e2e-verified.

**The constraint**: this handoff works only while legacy owns login-capable surfaces. → **OMH-460 must complete before home or any booking-flow page flips.** Phase 1 static pages are unaffected (notice/faq verified as the two _unguarded_ `/my-page` routes).

**Scope notes for when this ticket starts** (from the live legacy modal, captured 2026-07-03):

* 로그인/회원가입 modal: email + 계속 (step flow), 비회원 예약확인/문의 entry, social login ×4 (Kakao / Naver / Google / Apple), terms-consent footer notice.
* The consent documents the flows reference are split in legacy: sign-up step uses **100057/100060** (enum) while the social-signup terms step hard-codes **100003/100051** — a recorded data-consistency issue (see OMH-709 comment + `docs/migration/mobile-hana-notes.md`); resolve the canonical set with the decision owner before wiring v2 consent.
* The shell's visual gate (criterion F pattern, OMH-710 plan) intentionally EXCLUDES the login modal until this ticket ships its v2 counterpart — excluded by recorded decision `LOGIN-MODAL-DEFER-OMH460`, at which point it must join the modal-open-state captures.

author: Justin
text:
**Scope reduction — auth foundation extracted to Phase 2 (2026-07-03).**

The **auth foundation** — authed header (avatar + name dropdown + logout, user-info API), session-expiry handling, login modal, and session issuance — has been pulled OUT of this ticket into [**OMH-748**](https://ohmyjira.atlassian.net/browse/OMH-748) (Phase 2 / OMH-457).

**Why**: Phase 2 migrates all auth-gated My Page routes, which cannot render coherently with the anonymous header, and today's login-port handoff targets a guarded legacy route (`/my-page/booking-history`) that becomes v2 in Phase 2 — breaking the handoff loop. So the auth foundation is a Phase-2 prerequisite, not Phase-5 work. (Surfaced during the OMH-709/710 shell review; recorded in the OMH-457 Epic body + `docs/migration/v2-migration-plan.md` §7.)

**What stays here (OMH-460 / Phase 5)**: the **home page** migration and the **Angular decommission**.

**Build approach carried into OMH-748 (Justin 2026-07-03)**: ship v2 login in the same client-side form as legacy first (legacy already ships OAuth secrets client-side, so v2 matching is no worse) — email + all 4 social, no handoff, no half-state. The server-side secret relocation is **OMH-477** (client-bundle secrets / PG payload / OAuth — corrected 2026-07-03, was mistakenly written as OMH-650 which is the Node-18 build baseline), a **follow-up hardening for both apps, NOT a blocker**; OMH-477 scope must include web-pc.

text:
**(7/3) Note for Sharing: Summary of Teams Discussion between Zia and Tracy2**

* Based on the STG QA status update, most of the remaining issues were confirmed to be minor, mainly related to rounding and display.
* However, two critical issues were identified in the process of reflecting newly created contracts in the Contract Intelligence Dashboard:

    * **New Exclusive contracts:** Reflected in the DB immediately, but Current Left Allotment is not displayed on the Dashboard.
    * **New Shared contracts:** The contract data itself is not displayed on the Dashboard.
    
* Separate tickets have been created for both issues, and Tom is currently investigating the root causes.
* Since the root causes have not yet been identified, the full scope of impact cannot currently be determined. Therefore, it was decided that the current state is not appropriate for Planning QA.
* **Planning QA is on hold until these issues are resolved.**
* The development team was asked to share an update once the root causes have been identified and a clear fix timeline has been established.
